Documentation template (נוסח)

<- Back to Reading MAM-parsed-plus

Its first parameter is the “target” - what is being documented. The second parameter contains the documentation (anomalous forms, variant readings, uncertain readings, etc.).

{
    "tmpl_name": "נוסח",
    "tmpl_params": {
        "1": "וּבֵרְﬞכ֥וּ",
        "2": "א=וּבֵרֲכ֥וּ (חטף)"
    }
}

A target need not contain letters of Scripture text. The current target types without such letters are:

  • Spaces: " " (U+0020, ASCII space) in column E, or "__" in column C.
  • Paragraph and poetic-spacing markers: סס, ססס, פפ, פפפ, ר0, ר1, ר3, ר4.
  • Explicit absence of a paragraph break: מ:אין פרשה בתחילת פרק or מ:אין פרשה בתחילת פרק בספרי אמ״ת.
  • Punctuation: the literal string ׃ (U+05C3, Hebrew punctuation sof pasuq) or the template מ:פסק.
  • Inverted-nun signs: מ:נו״ן הפוכה.
  • Verse labels: מ:פסוק in column D.

A target can also wrap one of these forms in מ:הערה-2.

As mentioned above, consumers must accept a target consisting of exactly one ASCII space (U+0020), preserving it without trimming it to an empty string or rejecting it as empty. The current mpplus data has six such targets, all in column E: Deuteronomy 23:8; 2 Samuel 23:24; Ezra 2:69; and Nehemiah 3:2, 3:10, and 7:68.

For example, Deuteronomy 23:8 has this target:

{
  "tmpl_name": "נוסח",
  "tmpl_params": {
    "1": " ",
    "2": "ל=פסקא באמצע פסוק (פרשה סתומה)"
  }
}
